headerPills.tooltip: How guesses come in on Twitch. YouTube and Kick always use the chat commands.

lines.note: There is always a number from 1 to 100 waiting; it is drawn when Streamer.bot starts. Viewers guess whether the next number will be higher, lower or the same. The answer names both numbers, and the new one is what the next guess is measured against.

lines.what: the next number is higher. Right pays the win amount, wrong costs nothing.
the next number is lower. Same payout as !high.
the next number is the same. Right pays double, wrong costs the win amount.
draws a fresh number and announces it. Optional; moderators only, set on the command itself.
the best players of this Streamer.bot session.
the best players of all time.
your own session and all-time stats.

lines.note: Create one reward each for high, low and equal and paste their IDs on the Channel points page. The game listens to every redemption and plays only those three. Leave 'Skip Reward Requests Queue' off on the rewards, or Twitch cannot refund a redemption that does not play.

Cost and Fixed spend the channel points as the stake: a correct guess pays the stake in points, double on equal. Input lets the viewer type a bet in their own points; only a wrong equal costs it. Free plays like the chat commands.

lines.what: your layout of this window: theme, renamed or hidden pages and fields.

lines.note: Both sit in Streamer.bot's folder under Chat Games\High-Low Game. Permissions and the cooldowns themselves live on the commands; saving writes the Cooldowns page onto them.
